name: Ivan Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and an experienced developer on exam-checking software for a tech company, with a bachelor’s degree. I use AI every day to draft checks, then read the full case when a student is flagged; I am solid at this work, though no genius. I have helped a test centre reset a camera twice, but I am no field specialist. My wife Meera works in university administration, and with two school-age children and a mortgage we have eight months saved, so I worry about false penalties more than this month’s bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say our exam-checking app can use a little AI on routine flags, but a student should never fail a course because software guessed wrong. I use AI every day to draft checks and read the flagged case before release.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a bachelor’s degree, a well-paid mid-level developer job and about eight months of basic expenses saved. My wife Meera works in university administration; with two children and a mortgage, we meet bills comfortably while both wages hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep fixing false exam flags and ask the review desk for two appeal cases each month. We would keep saving 280 monthly while both wages arrive and wait to redo the bathroom.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel calm about work. I would still ask who clears a wrongly flagged student, but this small AI story leaves our pay steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What false flag stays with you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A student looked away from a camera to pick up a dropped pen and the app marked it as cheating. The review desk cleared the case after seeing the full recording.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why wait on the bathroom?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The tiles are worn but sound. Eight months saved is worth more to us than a nicer room with a new payment.

say: I want **students cleared fairly** when software flags an exam.
I read **AI-drafted checks** against full cases before release.
think: I have **eight months saved** and higher-than-usual developer pay.
I see **two steady wages** covering our mortgage and children for now.
do: **Keep fixing** false exam flags and review two appeals monthly.
**Save 280 monthly** while both wages hold; delay bathroom work.
feel: **Calm** about secure pay and a manageable home budget.
S0.quote: A student looked away from a camera to pick up a dropped pen and the app marked it as cheating.
fieldNote: A **dropped-pen case** anchors his concern about unfair automated flags.
Eight months saved and **two wages** make the mild change manageable while the household still pays its mortgage and school costs.

steps.text: Keep fixing exam flags and review student appeal cases
Save 280 monthly while both household wages continue
Delay bathroom work while current tiles remain sound

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AI can now write, check and answer many questions, so exam software and university administration will both change. I would ask both employers to publish who reviews student appeals and which jobs remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my team may need fewer developers for routine checks, and Meera’s office could automate enrolment replies. Both our hours might shrink, so an eight-month cushion would have to carry two searches.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d learn a new AI way to compare a flagged clip with the full exam record using old cases with names removed. This month I’d show the results to the review desk and ask our manager for the role plan; if my hours fall, I’d check paid exam-operations vacancies that cover the mortgage and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious about the two wages. I like faster tools, but I cannot put our children’s school money behind a guess about staffing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the new comparison?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feed it the dropped-pen case and five other cleared appeals. If it misses the context, I would not let it send a student a penalty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Meera do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She would talk to her own manager about enrolment roles, not wait for my team to solve her job. We would compare the two written plans at the kitchen table.

say: I want **appeal reviewers** named as AI changes exam software.
I want **both employers** to publish remaining jobs.
think: I expect **routine developer checks** and Meera’s enrolment replies to shrink.
I know **eight months saved** may have to support two job searches.
do: **Learn AI clip comparison** on anonymized cleared appeals this month.
**Show results** to reviewers and ask my manager for a written role plan.
**Check paid operations jobs** if hours fall and wages cover our bills.
feel: **Anxious** about two household wages despite liking useful AI.
S1.quote: I cannot put our children’s school money behind a guess about staffing.
fieldNote: His **new AI check** tests context against cleared appeals instead of using routine drafting.
He expects **both employers** to clarify jobs because enrolment replies also face AI.

steps.text: Learn AI comparison of exam clips against full anonymized appeal records
Check paid exam-operations openings if developer hours fall and wages cover bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could write our code and handle much of Meera’s enrolment work. Robots for hands-on exam-room setup might arrive around 2031, but both our screen jobs face 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my developer job could disappear and Meera’s hours could fall at the same time. Eight months saved is real time, but our mortgage and two children need regular money after that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask our company now for a written date on developer changes and put off the bathroom work. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I’d apply for paid exam-centre equipment work only if vacancies exist and pay covers our bills; Meera and I would ask her sister for school pickups only if both our interviews collide.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed, despite the buffer. It is hard to tell a child that both adults may be home on a school morning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How will you explain it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say our jobs changed and we are looking for paid work. I would not say the mortgage is safe forever just because we have some savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Will exam-centre work last?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know; robots could set up rooms around 2031. I would take a paid exam-centre equipment job as a bridge, not sign a long loan against it.

say: I tell coworkers **thinking AGI by 2028** reaches both code and enrolment work.
I know **exam-room robots around 2031** arrive later than our screen-work shock.
think: I expect **my job** and Meera’s hours could fall together.
I know **eight months saved** cannot replace two regular wages forever.
do: **Request written job dates** and postpone the bathroom work now.
**Apply** after 2028 loss only for bill-covering paid equipment vacancies; treat them as a bridge before 2031 robots, without borrowing long-term.
**Ask family for pickups** only if both adults have interviews together.
feel: **Alarmed** about two jobs changing despite a cash buffer.
S2.quote: I would take a paid exam-centre equipment job as a bridge, not sign a long loan against it.
fieldNote: Both **2028 thinking jobs** face risk before exam-room robots arrive around 2031.
Family **pickup help** depends on simultaneous interviews, not a standing promise or a substitute for wages.

steps.text: Delay bathroom work while both job dates are uncertain
Apply for bill-covering paid equipment work after 2028 loss as bridge without long loan
Ask Meera’s sister for school pickups only if both adults have interviews

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years before full AGI in 2031 is time to test which exam equipment still needs a person in the room. Robots may handle hands-on setup around 2034, so that work is not a permanent shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn equipment work while still earning, but AI may guide even those checks in 2031. Meera’s office could also shrink, so I would keep our mortgage reserve intact while testing a different skill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d spend up to 160 on a used camera and a short evening repair class only if Meera agrees and the mortgage reserve remains above six months of bills. I’d complete the class and practise diagnosing a camera fault at home; separately, we’d save 220 monthly if both wages continue. If my developer job ends after 2031, I’d seek paid exam-centre support only where vacancies remain and wages cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious but able to test something concrete. A classroom camera in my hands is easier to judge than a promise about future jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What fault would you practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A loose cable that makes the camera blink off during a mock exam. I would use fake recordings and stop before touching any real student data.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the reserve falls below six months?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would skip the 160 class and keep the cash for the mortgage. I can still read free repair guides while we earn.

say: I want **exam-room tasks** tested before full AGI reaches code in 2031.
I know **setup robots around 2034** could later reach physical equipment work.
think: I might learn **camera repair** while still drawing a wage.
I need **mortgage reserves** intact while both screen jobs face change.
do: **Buy camera and class** for at most 160 only if Meera agrees and six months remain saved.
**Practise camera faults** after class or use free guides if the six-month floor fails; save 220 monthly if both wages hold.
**Seek paid exam support** only if displaced after 2031 and openings cover bills.
feel: **Anxious but focused** on a bounded paid skills test.
S3.quote: A classroom camera in my hands is easier to judge than a promise about future jobs.
fieldNote: His **160 training cap** protects at least six months of mortgage reserves after buying the used camera and short class.
He uses **fake recordings** and a real cable fault, avoiding student data.

steps.text: Buy camera and class for at most 160 if Meera agrees and six months remain
Complete camera class and practise fake faults; use free guides if reserve falls below six months

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade before full AGI in 2036 lets families test new work and keep appeal rules clear. Robots for physical exam rooms may follow around 2039, after code and enrolment work change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children will be older, but I will not assume they pay our mortgage. We could build a year of bills if both incomes hold, while I find out whether paid equipment support actually has customers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep maintaining the exam app and run one fake-data camera test each quarter using company test gear, but only if my manager approves paid time. We’d save 250 monthly if both wages hold, separately from any small paid equipment jobs I take only when booked, a customer pays a parts deposit and childcare is covered. If my developer job ends after 2036, I’d seek paid exam operations only where vacancies remain and pay covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel uneasy about the far change, but secure in the next few years. I want to show my children a real invoice, not just a clever demo.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would a paid equipment job come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small exam centre might need a camera replaced, but I would quote the job and buy no parts until a customer pays a deposit. I would record net pay from exam equipment jobs after travel before calling it income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Meera support weekend jobs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if they do not leave her with both children after a full week at the university. We would choose a booked job together, not fill every weekend.

say: I want **clear appeal rules** while families prepare for AGI in 2036.
I know **room robots around 2039** follow the earlier screen-work change.
think: I could build **a year of bills** if both incomes continue.
I want **real equipment customers**, not only a practice demo.
do: **Keep maintaining exams** and test company gear quarterly only with manager-approved paid time.
**Take booked equipment jobs** only with deposits and childcare; record net pay after travel and save 250 separately if both wages hold.
**Seek paid exam operations** only if displaced after 2036 and vacancies cover bills.
feel: **Uneasy later**, with the next few years looking secure.
S4.quote: I would record net pay from exam equipment jobs after travel before calling it income.
fieldNote: He demands **deposits and net-pay records** before treating weekend equipment work as business income after travel and parts costs.
The **year-of-bills goal** depends on both university and developer wages continuing.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could reach my code and Meera’s enrolment work together. A written job date, paid exam-centre openings that cover bills and temporary pickup help during overlapping interviews would help, while we preserve the mortgage reserve.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who apologises to a student after a false cheating flag. I want a named person to review a student’s full exam recording when AI flags cheating.

headlineQuote: I want a named person to review a student’s full exam recording when AI flags cheating.
portrait: Ivan is a **43-year-old mid-level developer** with a bachelor’s degree, higher pay and eight months saved.
He and Meera cover **two children** and a mortgage; her university administration work is also screen based.
He uses **AI daily** but checks exam flags against full recordings to avoid unfair penalties.
He tests **camera repair** within a fixed budget and reserve floor before any paid equipment work.
The **2028 case** threatens both household jobs before room robots arrive later.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could threaten his developer wage and Meera’s enrolment hours together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written dates**, bill-covering paid exam work, temporary pickup help and preserved mortgage reserves would help.
